result.title: Sharing Resources at Work
result.objective: Learners will understand and correctly use allocate water to and in line with in workplace messages.

exercises.prompt: In s1, the team will allocate water to each plot according to the crops and the weekly forecast. What does allocate water to mean here?

options.text: It means the team will distribute and assign a share of water to each plot for use.
options.explanation: Correct because it matches the source meaning of distributing water to each plot.

options.text: It means the team will drain all water away from each plot to keep it dry.
options.explanation: Wrong because the team gives water to plots instead of removing it.

options.text: It means the team will drink the water together at each plot during a break.
options.explanation: Wrong because the water is for the crops, not for the team to drink.

exercises.explanation: Only option a fits the context of giving water to plots for crops.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses allocate water to naturally and correctly.

options.text: The manager will allocate water to each department kitchen every week.
options.explanation: Correct because it uses the right verb form and the fixed preposition to.

options.text: The manager will allocates water to each department kitchen every week.
options.explanation: Wrong because after will the verb should be allocate without s.

options.text: The manager will allocate water on each department kitchen every week.
options.explanation: Wrong because the fixed collocation requires to instead of on.

exercises.explanation: Only option a is grammatically correct and natural.

exercises.prompt: In s2, volunteers can adjust the schedule in line with changes in rainfall. What does in line with mean here?

options.text: It means the schedule agrees with or follows changes in rainfall.
options.explanation: Correct because it matches the source meaning of according to rainfall changes.

options.text: It means the schedule opposes changes in rainfall and ignores them.
options.explanation: Wrong because the schedule follows rainfall instead of opposing it.

options.text: It means the schedule stands in a physical line behind the rainfall.
options.explanation: Wrong because the phrase shows agreement, not physical position.

exercises.explanation: Only option a fits the context of adjusting to rainfall.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses in line with naturally and correctly.

options.text: The new schedule is in line with the updated safety rules.
options.explanation: Correct because it uses the fixed phrase in line with to show agreement.

options.text: The new schedule is in lines with the updated safety rules.
options.explanation: Wrong because the fixed noun should be singular line instead of lines.

options.text: The new schedule is in line of the updated safety rules.
options.explanation: Wrong because the fixed preposition should be with instead of of.

exercises.explanation: Only option a is grammatically correct and natural.

exercises.prompt: You are an office assistant writing a short note to colleagues about a change in break times. Write 2-3 sentences explaining the change and why it was made using the phrase in line with.
exercises.sampleAnswer: We have moved the lunch break to 12:30. This change is in line with the new working hours from head office.
selfCheck: I used in line with to show agreement with a rule or change.
My note is clear and correct for colleagues.
exercises.explanation: Compare with the model and self-assess; no automatic grade.
